# Release Notes v0.7.2

**Released:** 2026-10-21

This release makes the daemon quieter when nothing is watching and tougher when something goes wrong. The render loop now parks completely when no device, preview, or capture consumes frames, a new supervisor restarts the render pipeline in-process instead of taking the daemon down, and the Ableton Push 2 becomes a real input device with pads, touch strip, and buttons routed through the spatial layout. The default render target also moves from 30 to 60 fps.

## 🌟 Highlights

### 🎹 Push 2 Pads, Touch Strip, and Buttons as Device Input
The Push 2 driver now publishes input through its User port MIDI connection. All 64 pads report as contacts with velocity-derived pressure, the touch strip reports 14-bit position as contact 64, and 65 named buttons report press and release by snake_case name (`tap_tempo`, `select_1`..`select_8`, and the rest of the Spec 28 tables). New modules: `hypercolor-hal/src/drivers/push2/input.rs`, `protocol/input.rs`, and the `TransportInputSink` trait in `hypercolor-hal/src/transport/input.rs`.

### 📍 Per-Segment Touch Placement
`DeviceInputEdge::TouchBegan` now carries a `segment: Option<Arc<str>>` naming which device segment the contact landed on, so a touch on the Push 2 pad grid and a touch on its strip resolve through their own outputs in the spatial layout. `DeviceSurfaceMap::segment_canvas_position()` matches segment names exactly the way LED routing does, including case-insensitive alias matching via `slot_alias_key_matches` with no allocation on the frame path.

### 🛌 The Render Loop Parks When Nothing Consumes Frames
A new `OutputGate` counts live consumers (connected output devices, bus stream receivers, input event streams, explicit `OutputDemandHold`s) before each frame. With zero consumers and producers settled, the loop parks: no frames, no compositor work, no GPU draw, and render time stops advancing. It wakes on an `OutputDemandSignal` notification, a device registry change, a queued scene transaction, an input demand change, or a 1-second safety tick, and resumes at its current fps tier with no catch-up frames.

### 🛡️ Supervised Render Pipeline with In-Process Restart
`render_thread/supervisor.rs` and `supervision.rs` catch render pipeline panics, terminated input pumps, and failed rebuilds, then restart the pipeline in-process under a budget (5 restarts in 300s, exponential backoff from 250ms to 8s, reset after 60s of stable uptime). Exhausting the budget or losing the GPU device exits the daemon nonzero so systemd or the Windows service manager restarts it. Failures persist to `render-failure.json` so they survive log loss and `panic = "abort"` builds.

### ⚡ Preview Streaming Without WASM Round Trips
Chunked preview frames reassemble with payload bytes staying in JS. Only the fixed-size chunk envelope crosses the WASM boundary, cutting per-frame copies into WASM from roughly 1.23 MB to 124 bytes on a 640x480 canvas and removing the copy back out entirely. Combined with removing per-frame closure allocation in the `requestAnimationFrame` scheduler and the preview expiry timer, FinalizationRegistry registrations on the Effects page drop from about 67.5/s to 0.12/s.

## 🤖 Device Input

- Pad pressure is floored at strike velocity: holding a pad reports `max(strike_velocity, latest_aftertouch)` so pressure no longer collapses to zero once aftertouch settles
- `MAX_CONTACTS_PER_DEVICE` raised from 32 to 128 so a Push 2 holding 65 simultaneous contacts (64 pads plus the strip) never drops input
- Touch strip autoreturn is disambiguated: a center pitch bend value only moves the touch when the finger is still down
- `DeviceInputPublisher::renew()` replaces an input lease atomically on the host, cancelling held input; stale leases return `None`
- A superseded USB input bridge can never take a device back. `UsbDeviceInput` tracks a `Pending` → `Live` → `Closed` lease and `publish()` returns `false` once superseded
- `InputEvent::Touch` gains an optional `segment` field, omitted from JSON when absent. SDK `TouchContact` docs now state that surface x/y are in the segment's LED frame, not physical layout
- Driver-owned USB transports can publish device input directly

## 🎬 Render Pipeline

- Displays keep their own zone's backdrop. Scene composition now runs in two strata, LED outputs in zone order first, then display backdrops, so a later zone's effect layer no longer paints over an LCD placed by an earlier zone (Spec 86 §5.1 documents the display-last order)
- `EffectRenderer` gains `park()` to quiesce background work (web effects stop their `requestAnimationFrame` loops) and `is_warming()` to hold the loop open while an HTML page is still loading
- `EffectPool::park()` and `EffectPool::any_warming()` propagate that across every renderer
- Uncaptured wgpu errors are counted and burst-limit logged instead of panicking the thread. Device loss stays a sticky, fatal signal that triggers process restart
- A process-wide panic hook records every thread panic with a trimmed backtrace excerpt, bounded to 48 frames and 12 KiB
- Park telemetry clears whenever a pipeline starts, and a restart is only published together with the failure behind it

## 🔍 Diagnostics and Status

- `/api/v1/system` gains `render_loop.output_demand` (`parked`, `idle_reason`, `parked_ms`, `output_devices`, `stream_receivers`, `input_event_streams`, `demand_holds`, `parks_total`, `last_wake_reason`)
- `SystemStatus` gains `render_supervision` with `phase`, `restarts_total`, `consecutive_failures`, `max_restarts`, `last_frame_age_ms`, `last_failure` (`RenderFailureStatus`), and `gpu_errors` (`GpuErrorStatus`)
- `hypercolor status` prints `parked` as the fps health word instead of a failing `0%`, plus a line explaining that nothing renders until a device, preview, or capture appears
- New diagnose checks: `render_thread_check` (stall, restart, phase mismatch) and `gpu_errors_check` (warns on uncaptured errors within 10 minutes, fails on device loss). Render stalls are now measured from when frames were due again, and parked loops are judged by poll age rather than frame age
- Private diagnostic messages, source locations, and last GPU error details are withheld unless `include_private_diagnostics` is set
- `output_power_snapshot` renames the output power read for clarity
- Python client regenerated with `RenderOutputDemandStatus`, `RenderSupervisionStatus`, `RenderFailureStatus`, and `GpuErrorStatus` models

## 🖥️ Web UI

- Previews unsubscribe while the page is hidden. The old 6 fps hidden-tab cap is gone, taking background traffic from about 7.1 MB/s to zero on an idle tab
- Canvas, screen-canvas, and web-viewport preview effects now wait for `ConnectionState::Connected` before subscribing, and clear recorded requests while connecting or closing. This fixes a dark preview that persisted after any socket reconnect, including macOS wake in the desktop app
- Only preview streams that were actually requested are unsubscribed
- Ambient tint moves off the frame path: `--ambient-l`, `--ambient-c`, and alpha tokens resolve the tint once on `:root`, while `.preview-glow` drifts its own `--ambient-hue-drift` without triggering document-wide repaints. The drift now starts from the hue CSS already holds
- Preview reassembly budgets are measured against the native `PreviewStreamState<Vec<u8>>` layout for every storage backend, so the browser client admits exactly the same stream count as native clients
- Reassembled previews that fail to decode are now logged instead of silently dropped

## 🔊 Audio

- System-audio capture no longer opens the microphone unasked on macOS. `microphone_record_permission()` reads `AVAudioApplication.recordPermission()` without prompting, and the default-input fallback only proceeds when permission is `Granted` or `NotRequired`
- New `AudioInputPermission` enum (`Granted`, `Denied`, `Undetermined`, `NotRequired`) in `hypercolor-types`
- New failure kind `audio_loopback_unavailable` with remediation text pointing at audio settings. A refused fallback degrades the source in place and retries on the normal recovery cadence rather than aborting the reconfiguration

## 🎉 First-Run Experience

- Fresh installs seed the active scene's primary zone with **Hyperbloom** and favorite five effects that look good with no devices attached: `hyperbloom`, `borealis`, `bubble-garden`, `plasma-engine`, `spectral-fire`
- Seeding is skipped entirely if any runtime session, named-scene store, or library store already exists, so upgrades are untouched
- `bundled_html_effect_id(stem)` derives a stable `hypercolor:html-bundled:{stem}` id so bundled effects resolve identically across installs and platforms

## 👷 Build, CI, and Security

- Bumped `rustls-webpki` to 0.103.16 and the `webpki-roots` / `webpki-root-certs` bundles to 1.0.10 for RUSTSEC-2026-0382 and RUSTSEC-2026-0383 (distrusted emSign intermediate private keys are public)
- Release CI builds only `--bin hypercolor-daemon` on macOS and Windows. Three dev tool binaries were each paying a full fat-LTO link over Servo for nothing, costing 201 minutes on macOS and 72 on Windows
- `cargo-binstall` for `tauri-cli` now passes `GITHUB_TOKEN`, avoiding rate-limit fallback to a ten-minute source build
- `install-windows-service.ps1` sets `sc.exe failureflag 1` so the configured restart actions fire on a clean nonzero exit, not just on a crash
- Linux `spawn_watchdog_while(healthy)` withholds the systemd keepalive when the daemon reports itself unhealthy
- Panic backtrace excerpts now cut at std's `__rust_end_short_backtrace` marker, start at the panicking frame on Windows, and stop the skip at the first unrecognized frame

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

- **Config schema 7.** `CURRENT_SCHEMA_VERSION` moves from 6 to 7 and `daemon.target_fps` defaults to 60. The `migrate_v6_to_v7` step drops a `target_fps` that is still exactly `30` (the retired v6 default) so the new default applies; any other value was chosen deliberately and is preserved. Schemas 4 through 7 are still readable and upgrade in memory. `packaging/managed/durable-stores.json` now records `readable_schema_max: 7` and `written_schema: 7`.
- **`DeviceInputEdge::TouchBegan` gains a required `segment` field.** Driver and consumer code that constructs or matches on this variant must be updated. `InputEvent::Touch` adds a matching optional `segment` field to its JSON payload.
- **`MAX_CONTACTS_PER_DEVICE` raised from 32 to 128.** Code that sized buffers against the old bound should be rechecked.
- **Transports must renew a lease through `interrupted()`.** A bridge whose lease was superseded now gets `false` from `publish()` and cannot reclaim the device.

## 📝 Upgrade Notes

- Expect a config rewrite on first start: schema 6 files upgrade to 7 in memory, and a `target_fps` of exactly 30 is dropped so the 60 fps default applies. Set `daemon.target_fps = 30` explicitly if you want the old cadence.
- An idle daemon with no devices, previews, or captures now reports 0 fps and `parked` in `hypercolor status`. That is expected, not a failure. Check `render_loop.output_demand` on `/api/v1/system` if you need to know why.
- On macOS, system-audio capture no longer silently falls back to the microphone. If audio stops reacting, grant microphone permission or pick a loopback input in audio settings; the daemon reports `audio_loopback_unavailable` with remediation text.
- Windows service installs should re-run `scripts/install-windows-service.ps1` so `failureflag` is set and restart actions apply to nonzero exits.
- Drivers implementing `DeviceInputPublisher` or consuming `DeviceInputEdge` need updating for the new `segment` field and the optional `renew()` method.
- Fresh installs get Hyperbloom plus five seeded favorites. Existing installs with any saved session, scene, or library state are left alone.
